interface.name: kde_stereo_content_manager_v1
interface.description:
A program tells the compositor that a surface's picture holds two views packed full side by side, with the left view first. The compositor renders the declared surface using each view. The global being present announces support.
Since version 3, a program may also follow a surface's desktop depth with get_depth, to draw the elements inside the surface at their own depths.
Clients may use this protocol to declare stereo content. The version 1 wire values are stable; future requests must use a new interface version. Destroying the manager does not affect declarations it created.

request.name: create

description.summary: Create a stereo content declaration for a surface

request.description: Creates a kde_stereo_content_v1 object for the given surface. The declaration is none until set_content is called. If the surface already has a declaration, the already_declared error is raised.

entry.name: already_declared
entry.summary: the surface already has a stereo content declaration

request.name: get_depth

description.summary: Follow and describe a surface's desktop depth

request.description: Creates a kde_stereo_depth_v1 object for the given surface. A surface may have any number of them, made by any part of the client, such as a toolkit and its style, and independently of its stereo content declaration.

interface.name: kde_stereo_content_v1

description.summary: stereo content declaration of one surface

interface.description:
The declaration of one surface, created with kde_stereo_content_manager_v1.create.
Since version 2, a surface declared side_by_side_full is one view wide and its buffer holds both views: unless a wp_viewport destination is set, the surface's size is half the width the buffer would give it (after the buffer scale, the buffer transform and a viewport source) by the full height. A viewport destination, when set, is the size of one view. With version 1 the surface's size follows its buffer as for any other surface, so a client that declares at version 1 maps the buffer onto one view's size itself, for example with a viewport.
Version 3 changes nothing in this interface. Version 4 adds a double-buffered native source rectangle for each view.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Resets the content to none on the next wl_surface commit. The surface may receive a new declaration immediately.

enum.name: content

description.summary: full side-by-side packing of the two views

enum.description: The value matches the X11 property _KDE_NET_WM_STEREO_CONTENT.

entry.name: side_by_side_full
entry.summary: side by side, native width per view, left first

request.name: set_content
request.description: Takes effect with the next commit of the surface. Unknown values are treated as none. Declaring none clears the format and does not destroy the declaration object.

request.name: set_view_source

description.summary: select the same native source rectangle in both views

request.description:
Select a rectangle independently within each view of side_by_side_full content. Coordinates are native buffer pixels after the buffer transform, relative to the top left of each half of the viewport source rectangle. The viewport destination remains the logical size of one drawing area. No new packing or view-order value is introduced.
The rectangle is double buffered with wl_surface.commit. Initially it is unset. Set all four values to -1 to unset it. Otherwise x and y must be nonnegative and width and height strictly positive. The rectangle must fit inside each view when a buffer is committed; otherwise bad_source is raised. With no viewport destination, the rectangle's size divided by buffer scale gives the surface size. Fractional edges are retained.
Setting content to none or destroying the declaration also unsets the rectangle. This request on a destroyed wl_surface raises no_surface. Existing clients which do not set a view source keep their behavior.

interface.name: kde_stereo_depth_v1
interface.description:
The compositor shows the desktop's own surfaces at depth levels: the active window at the screen, the windows lying behind it sunk, menus, tooltips and popups popped. This object lets a client show depth inside a surface as well, by drawing the surface's elements once per view at their own depths and handing the two views over full side by side, declared with kde_stereo_content_v1:
- the compositor tells the client when the elements inside the surface may be shown in depth, and which of the surface's edges lie on its output's edge; - the client marks such a pair as the desktop's own depth rather than stereo content; - a popup surface may declare its place.
The depth limits are the user's settings; the client reads them itself.
A surface may have any number of these objects. The depth state is sent to each of them. The surface is marked as desktop depth while any of its objects marks it, and its place is the one set most recently by any of its objects that has one.
When the surface is destroyed, the object becomes inert: its requests are ignored and no further event is sent.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The desktop depth mark and the place this object set are withdrawn on the next wl_surface commit.

event.name: depth_state

description.summary: Whether the surface may show depth inside it now

event.description:
Sent once after the object is created and again whenever either value changes.
awake is nonzero while elements drawn inside the surface may be shown in depth: the surface is on an output that shows stereo, and it is awake, as the active window on top of what it overlaps, a popup, a panel or a desktop widget is, rather than one of the windows lying flat behind the active one. While the surface is not awake the client draws it as for a 2D output.
output_edges are the edges of the surface, for a window those of its frame, that touch an edge of its output. Nothing at such an edge comes nearer than the screen.

arg.name: awake
arg.summary: nonzero while depth may be shown inside the surface

arg.name: output_edges
arg.summary: the surface's edges on its output's edge

request.name: set_desktop_depth

description.summary: Mark the surface's pair as the desktop's own depth

request.description:
Nonzero marks the full side-by-side pair the surface shows, declared with kde_stereo_content_v1 by this client or its graphics library, as the desktop's own elements drawn once per view rather than stereo content: where the compositor treats stereo content differently, for example in switching a display into a 3D mode, in stereo screenshots or in estimating the depth of content, the surface counts as part of the desktop. The compositor still presents each view separately. Zero withdraws the mark.
Takes effect with the next wl_surface commit.

arg.name: desktop_depth
arg.summary: nonzero marks the pair, zero withdraws the mark

request.name: set_place

description.summary: Declare the place of a popup surface

request.description:
Declares where a popup surface (a menu, tooltip, popup or dialog) sits in depth, as a fraction of the user's limits: -1 is the sunk limit, 0 the screen and 1 the popped limit; values beyond are limited to that range. The compositor places the surface there under its own rules: a surface at its output's edge stays at the screen, and a popup is never behind the surface it was opened from. Without a place the compositor places the surface itself. The place of a surface that is not a popup is ignored.
Takes effect with the next wl_surface commit.

arg.name: depth
arg.summary: the place, from -1 to 1 of the user's limits

request.name: unset_place
request.description: Withdraws the place this object set. Takes effect with the next wl_surface commit.
